“I worried refusal would hurt the relationship, so I tried a joke. I do not want my apology to become consent.”

You are drawing a useful line between repairing tone and conceding substance: the apology addressed the joke, while the limit about tracking stayed intact — and Ning explicitly confirmed the limit stands. That shows an apology can acknowledge impact without functioning as agreement, which is exactly the risk you flagged. It also suggests your worry that refusal would damage things did not hold up in the transcript, since he stayed engaged and even proposed naming future disagreements calmly.

Clarifying follow-up: you said the joke 'may sound dismissive' — do you think the limit itself, or only the joking delivery, was what risked hurting him? Distinguishing those two would help you apologize for tone in future without ever casting doubt on the boundary.
